newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars firm ahead employment cost index.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars firm ahead employment cost index.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended on a firm note on Tuesday ahead of the release of the U.S. quarterly employment cost index (ECI), known to be a key indicator in setting Federal Reserve policy.
"Greenspan has given a very optimistic view of the economy and he'll want to see whether there are any inflationary pressures in this number," a trader at an Asian house said.
He was referring to Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony last week, which suggested the U.S. economy was still charting healthy growth with no immediate threat of inflation.
"Eurodollars have been picking up good buying from yesterday. U.S. treasuries are lending good support to the market," the trader said.
The second quarter ECI, due at 1230 GMT, is expected to rise by 0.8 percent after a 0.6 percent increase in the first quarter, according to the consensus in a Reuters survey.
A dealer at a U.S. futures house said December Eurodollars could rally to 94.25 if the ECI figure was market-friendly. On the downside, he said the contract would be supported at 94.05.
It ended at 94.150 against an IMM close at 94.140.

Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures backed off a bit after some damaging comments by a former Japanese Ministry of Finance (MOF) official, but dealers said the market was cautious ahead of Japan's June industrial output data.
Japan's industrial output, due on Wednesday, is expected to have fallen 2.8 percent in June from the previous month after rising 4.5 percent in May, according to economists' forecasts.

A dealer at a European house said JGB futures came under pressure after Makoto Utsumi, former MOF vice-minister for international affairs, said JGBs were trading at "bubble" levels and prices were likely to see a downward correction.
September JGBs ended at 125.76 against a previous 125.79 after trading to a high of 125.92.
The lead March Euroyen contract was stuck in a one-tick band and stood at 99.10 at 1118 GMT against its IMM close at 99.11.
Support is seen at 99.05 and resistance around 99.15.
